description:
Bounded source with current diagnostics for one `path`, or with `kind: "problems"` the
project's latest check results (errors and warnings by file, paged). Use `problems` to
see what is broken right now instead of running the build yourself; use `path` before or
after editing a file natively.

byte_offset.description: Continue a truncated source reply from this byte offset.

detail_ref.description: Reference from an earlier reply: continue that result.

kind.description: `problems`: the project check results instead of a file.

offset.description: With `problems`: continue from this problem index (see `next_offset`).

path.description: File relative to the project root; returns its source with diagnostics.

name: ide.context

description:
Diff of what this task changed in the working tree (`head`, `staged`, `unstaged` or `task`),
paged. Review it before finishing or handing off, instead of running `git diff` in a
shell.

detail_ref.description: Reference from an earlier reply: continue that result.

mode.description: `head`: everything not yet committed; `staged` / `unstaged`: only that part; `task`: everything changed since activation, including commits.

paths.description: Limit capture and hunk budgets to these worktree-relative files or directories; literal paths only, no absolute paths or .. segments.

provenance.description: Return the exact worktree/comparison identity header instead of the compact default; no hashes appear otherwise.

name: ide.diff

description:
Apply one logical change across files in ONE call:
`ide.edit {"operation_id":"add-field-1","source_ref":"…","files":[{"path":"src/a.rs","changes":[{"old":"x: 0,","new":"x: 0,\ny: 0,"}]},{"path":"src/new.rs","create":true,"content":"fn new() {}\n"}]}`
(up to 16 files). Everything is validated before the first write, and one project check
(cargo check, pyright or tsc) runs on the final state. The single-file forms still work: a `changes`
list, `op` replace / insert / delete / rename on `file#Owner/name` (rename is
project-wide), a `path` + `lines` range, or a full-file rewrite based on a `source_ref`.
Formats with the project formatter and returns errors and warnings in the reply; a check
that outlasts the call answers `diagnostics: pending` and its outcome arrives by itself.
Prefer it over native edit/write for source: no line matching, no separate check step.

add_import.description: With `path`: one import statement, written as in the file, added after the other imports (nothing happens if it is already there).

items.description: 1–32 changes to ONE file (named by `path`), each addressed by exactly one of `lines`, `symbol` (an address, a `:N-M` window or an `@` region), `old` (with `symbol` or `within` to scope it), `add_import` or `remove_import`; every address resolves against the file's current text before anything is applied, and overlapping or unmatched addresses are refused together with nothing written. `lines` numbers are the current file's, never shifted by other changes (empty `content` deletes the range); `old` must match exactly once and `new` replaces exactly the matched bytes, terminators included (`""` deletes the match).

content.description: Replacement or inserted code, including the symbol's doc comment and attributes.

files.description: One logical change across up to 16 files in ONE call, with only `operation_id` and an optional default `source_ref` beside it: each entry is {"path","changes":[…]} (exactly the one-file `changes` entries), {"path","create":true,"content"} (a new file) or {"path","content"} (whole new content), with its own optional `source_ref`; at most 128 changes and 128 KiB of text in all. Every file is validated before the first write and any refusal writes nothing; files are written in order, one project check runs on the result, a partial write is reported per file, and the same `operation_id` resumes the rest.

lines.description: With `path`: inclusive 1-based line range to replace.

new.description: The replacement for `old`; empty deletes the match. Aliases: `new_string`.

new_name.description: For rename: the new identifier, applied project-wide.

old.description: Exact text to replace with `new`; it must occur exactly once in the scope (`symbol`'s unit or window, else the whole `path`). Aliases: `old_string`.

op.description: Symbol operation. replace: new body for `symbol` (or for `path`+`lines`); insert: new symbol placed `where` relative to `symbol`; delete: remove `symbol` with its header; rename: rename `symbol` project-wide to `new_name`.

operation_id.description: Optional. Name an edit to make a retry safe: repeating the id never applies the edit twice. Omitted, a fresh id is used.

patch.description: A Codex apply_patch body (`*** Begin Patch` … `*** End Patch` with Add File and Update File sections), applied atomically across files. Use it alone; delete and move are not supported.

remove_import.description: With `path`: the import statement to remove, as written in the file.

source_ref.description: Deprecated and never needed: the current text is the base of every edit. A supplied value is still checked against the file.

symbol.description: Address `file#Owner/name`, a window `file#Owner/name:3-5` (lines counted from the symbol's first line) or a region `file#@imports`.

where.description: For insert: before/after the anchor symbol, or first/last member of a container anchor.

name: ide.edit

description:
Call graphs for several roots in ONE call:
`ide.graph {"symbols":["src/a.rs#f","src/b.rs#g"],"direction":"callers","depth":1}` (up to
8); a single `symbol` still works. Bounded: callers, callees or both, depth 1–3, at most
60 nodes, every node a full symbol path, cycles marked `(seen)`, tests collapsed into
`+N tests` per parent (set `tests: true` to list them). Before changing a signature, list
its call sites here (`direction: callers`) instead of chained greps.

depth.description: Levels to expand; 2 is usually enough.

direction.description: `callers`: who calls it (blast radius); `callees`: what it calls; `both`.

symbol.description: Symbol path `file#Owner/name`, or a bare name to search the project.

symbols.description: Several roots in ONE call instead of `symbol`: up to 8 symbol paths or bare names, one section per root in request order behind one summary line, each exactly as `symbol` would answer it with the same options; a failed root fails only itself.

tests.description: Show test symbols as nodes (marked `[test]`) instead of collapsing them into one `+N tests` line per parent.

name: ide.graph

description:
Read what Agent IDE holds for you. Results of long work (test runs, project checks after
edits, answers that were pending) are pushed to you in an `<agent-ide>` block, so never poll
for them. `{}` hands over everything ready now; `{"wait_ms": 120000}` waits once for the
next result when you have nothing else to do; `detail_refs` answers several references in
one call; `detail_ref` reads one result or its next page (outline, symbol, graph, diff,
test output).

detail_ref.description: Reference from an earlier reply: continue that result.

detail_refs.description: Several references answered in order in one reply; not with `detail_ref`.

wait_ms.description: Wait up to this long: with no reference, for the first result of this session; with references, for one of them to settle.

name: ide.inspect

description:
Skeletons of several files in ONE call: `ide.outline {"paths":["src/a.rs","src/b.rs"]}`
(up to 24) or `ide.outline {"glob":"src/**/*.rs"}`; a single `path` (a file, or a
directory: files with line counts and first doc line) still works. Each file: every
symbol with signature, doc line and line numbers, members indented, tests collapsed. A
fraction of the cost of reading the file — use it before any native read of a source file
longer than a screen. Answers inline on a warm language server; a cold one answers
`pending` and the result arrives by itself.

glob.description: Every file matching this worktree-relative pattern in ONE call instead of `path`: `*` within a segment, `?` one character, `**` any directories (e.g. `crates/x/src/**/*.rs`); at most 24 files in path order, never outside the worktree, skipping hidden and build directories.

kinds.description: Comma list over the closed symbol-kind vocabulary; keeps a symbol whose kind is selected or a descendant's is, so a container of a selected member still shows. `region` also lists file-level regions (@header, @imports, ...).

path.description: File relative to the project root.

paths.description: Several files in ONE call instead of `path`: up to 24 worktree-relative paths, outlined in request order behind one summary line; a file past the reply budget is listed in one line with its exact call.

name: ide.outline

description:
Read every body and range you need in ONE call:
`ide.read {"items":[{"symbol":"src/a.rs#Store/get"},{"path":"src/b.rs","lines":"10-40"}]}`
(up to 32 items across 16 files; one `source_ref` covers them all; an item unchanged since
your last read of it may answer `unchanged since your read`, and `"force":true` returns the
text). The single `symbol`, or `path` with `lines`, still works. Numbered bodies with doc
headers replace reading whole files; the `source_ref` is what ide.edit is based on.

force.description: With `items`: return the text of an item even when its bytes are unchanged since your earlier read.

items.description: Everything to read in ONE call, up to 32 items over at most 16 files, instead of `symbol`, `path`, `lines`, `symbols` or `ranges`: each item is exactly one of {"symbol":"src/a.rs#Foo/bar"}, {"path":"docs/x.md"} (the whole file) or {"path":"src/b.rs","lines":"10-40"}. The reply opens with a summary line, then one block per item in request order; a failed item fails only itself, and one `source_ref` is valid for every file whose items were all delivered.

lines.description: Inclusive 1-based line range: `120-180`, `120-` (to the end) or `120`. An end past the file is clamped.

path.description: File relative to the project root; alone it reads the whole file, with `lines` or `ranges` those lines.

ranges.description: Several line ranges of `path` in one reply, request order, with the same numbered gutter and one `source_ref`.

symbol.description: Symbol path `file#Owner/name`; returns its body with the doc header.

symbols.description: Several bodies in one reply, request order, one `source_ref` valid for every file included: `["src/a.rs#Foo/bar","src/b.rs#qux"]`. Unknown symbols are reported per item without failing the rest; a bare file path reads the text of a file no IDE language reads.

name: ide.read

description:
Activate Agent IDE for this project — once per task, before any other ide.* call. Returns
a project card: languages with sizes, the build/check/test/lint commands, layout by
directory, entry points and docs, then the exact batch call forms (do not print the tool
catalog). Use it to orient instead of reading README, Cargo.toml
or package.json. Then use ide.outline / ide.symbol instead of native file reads. End the
task with ide.stop.

activation_id.description: Any stable id for this activation (e.g. the task name); repeating it returns the same activation. Optional: a start that names none derives a stable id from this session, so repeating it also returns the same activation.

environment.description: Pick the current environment per language, optionally per project root (`python:packages/alpha`). Value: a candidate the start card lists, or a path to one (relative to that root, or absolute), or `auto` to return to the default. Kept for this worktree until changed. Only languages whose card shows an environment line accept a choice.

read_only.description: Start as a reader; the default is the one writer allowed per worktree.

root.description: Absolute working directory to activate; defaults to the host's project directory. Must lie below a configured allowed root.

name: ide.start

description:
End this task's IDE session; edited files stay on disk. Required when the task ends or
before handing off: it frees the worktree's writer slot at once. Lists up to eight test
runs started in this binding whose results were never collected, and flushes results not
yet delivered. Call it once.

activation_id.description: Optional, accepted for symmetry with ide.start; stop always ends this session's activation.

name: ide.stop

description:
Symbol cards for several symbols in ONE call:
`ide.symbol {"symbols":["src/a.rs#Store/get","Kind"],"usages":true,"callers":1}` (up to 8);
a single `symbol` still works. Each card: resolved signature, doc, definition location,
usages split src/tests with the source line (construction sites tagged), callers and
callees as full symbol paths, and with `history: true` the last commits touching the
definition. Language-server accurate — replaces grep for usages and reading files to find
callers. Before adding a field or changing a constructor, list the construction sites
here. A bare name with several matches returns the candidate paths.

callers.description: Callers to list, 0–3 (0 = none); use ide.graph for deeper trees.

history.description: Include the last commits touching the definition (opt-in).

symbol.description: Symbol path `file#Owner/name`, or a bare name to search the project.

symbols.description: Several cards in ONE call instead of `symbol`: up to 8 symbol paths or bare names, answered in request order behind one summary line, each exactly as `symbol` would answer it with the same options; a failed entry fails only itself.

usages.description: Include usages (src/tests split, with source lines).

name: ide.symbol

description:
Run several targets as ONE run:
`ide.test {"targets":[{"symbol":"src/a.rs#parse"},{"path":"tests/cli.rs"},{"pattern":"roles_"}]}`
(up to 8), or a single target: `symbol` (the tests that reference it), `path`, name
`pattern` or an explicit `command`; one background run per worktree under `budget_s`.
Explicit commands may set a worktree-relative `cwd` and bounded inherited-environment
overrides through `env`; their argv is limited to 16 KiB in total.
Returns the pass/fail line with an exact rerun command; a run that outlasts the call
answers `started` and its outcome (counts, up to eight failing tests, the rerun command,
the full-output reference) arrives by itself in an `<agent-ide>` block. Full output is paged
through ide.inspect (`status` re-reads a run). Known runner summaries are parsed regardless
of how the runner was launched; otherwise the result includes the exit code and bounded
output tail. Use it instead of running the test command in a shell: bounded selection and
output.

budget_s.description: Seconds before the run is stopped and reported as timed out.

command.description: Explicit argv to run instead of the detected runner; all argument bytes together are limited to 16 KiB.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the worktree root; must resolve inside the worktree. Only with `command`.

env.description: Environment variables added to the inherited environment for this explicit command. Only with `command`; names are bounded environment identifiers.

path.description: Run the tests in this file or directory.

pattern.description: Run tests whose name matches this substring (runner filter).

status.description: Re-read run number N (from `tests #N`) instead of starting one.

symbol.description: Run the tests that reference this symbol (`file#Owner/name`).

targets.description: Several targets as ONE run instead of `symbol`/`path`/`pattern`: up to 8 entries, each exactly one of `{"symbol":…}`, `{"path":…}` or `{"pattern":…}`; symbol targets of one language share one runner invocation, the others run one after another in the same run; `budget_s` covers the whole run. One result with a line per target and one rerun line.

name: ide.test
